nodes.label: Cap/Floor Volatility Structure
nodes.rationale: UseEffectiveVolatility distinguishes stripped vs effective overnight-caplet volatilities so the correct decay adjustment is applied; ORE supports interpolating on term vs optionlet volatilities depending on the granularity of available market data.

nodes.label: Proxy Cap Floor Volatility Configuration
nodes.rationale: Lets a well-calibrated surface for one index (e.g. USD-LIBOR-3M) be reused to build a surface for a related index (e.g. USD-SOFR) via forward-rate adjustment and optional scaling, when direct market quotes for the target index are unavailable.

nodes.label: CommodityCurve
nodes.rationale: Modelled as price curves (returning a price for time t) rather than discount-factor curves, matching how commodities are naturally quoted via futures/forward prices.

nodes.label: PriceSegment
nodes.rationale: Piecewise construction lets a single curve blend daily futures at the short end with monthly averaging futures at the long end, common in power markets.

nodes.label: APO (Average Price Option) Volatility Surface
nodes.rationale: Built from an existing futures-option volatility surface because direct market volatilities for average price options are typically unavailable.

nodes.label: Commodity Calendar Spread Option Volatility
nodes.rationale: Uses Normal (Bachelier) volatilities rather than lognormal because the underlying calendar spread price can be negative.

nodes.label: Default Curve from CDS
nodes.rationale: ImplyDefaultFromMarket lets ORE approximate pricing during the gap between a determined credit event and its auction settlement date, when recovery-rate quotes persist but spread/upfront quotes stop being published.

nodes.label: Benchmark Default Curve
nodes.rationale: Backs out an implied default/credit curve from the spread between an all-in bond-fitted discounting curve and a benchmark funding curve, useful for issuers without a liquid CDS market.

nodes.label: Default Curve from YieldCurve
nodes.rationale: Reinterprets a funding spread curve as a credit/default curve for reuse in pricers that consume default curves.

nodes.label: Fitted Bond Segment
nodes.rationale: Fits a parametric curve (Nelson-Siegel/Svensson/Exponential Splines) to a basket of liquid bond prices, for issuers/currencies lacking swap-based instruments.

nodes.label: Bond Yield Shifted Segment
nodes.rationale: Preferred over the Fitted Bond segment when only one or a few liquid bonds are available, since Nelson-Siegel fitting becomes unstable with too few calibration points.

nodes.label: Discount Ratio Segment
nodes.rationale: Assumes FX forward rates collateralised in one currency equal those collateralised via a common base currency, allowing construction of a cross-collateralised discount curve without direct quotes for that specific collateral pair.

nodes.label: Horizon Shift / Change of Measure
nodes.rationale: Placing the LGM shift horizon in the middle of the portfolio duration significantly improves numerical stability of long-horizon exposure expectations by counteracting convexity-driven drift in the simulated rate distribution.

nodes.label: Par Sensitivity Analysis (Jacobi transform)
nodes.rationale: Raw sensitivities are computed in a computationally convenient domain (zero rates, optionlet vols) but hedging requires fair-rate sensitivities; the Jacobi chain-rule transform converts between the two without repricing against par instruments directly.

nodes.label: Gabillon Model (Commodity)
nodes.rationale: The single-factor version is used as a practical simplification; the richer two-factor extension with time-dependent multiplier for accurate option calibration is noted as still to follow.

nodes.label: Margin Period of Risk (MPoR)
nodes.rationale: ORE prefers the Close-out (auxiliary-grid) approach over the legacy Lagged approach because it removes the requirement for equally-spaced time grids matching the MPoR and supports more detailed close-out value modelling (sticky vs actual date).
